title: Limhi and Ammon address the people
summary: After finishing his speech, King Limhi tells his people about their brethren in Zarahemla. He has Ammon stand before the multitude. Ammon recounts what happened to their brethren from Zeniff’s departure until his own arrival, then rehearses and explains King Benjamin’s last words.

explicit_facts.text: King Limhi finishes speaking to his people and tells them about their brethren in the land of Zarahemla.
King Limhi causes Ammon to stand before the multitude and recount what happened to their brethren from Zeniff’s departure until Ammon’s arrival.
Ammon rehearses King Benjamin’s last words and explains them to Limhi’s people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Limhi’s people are gathered as Ammon stands before them.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, clothing, and physical appearances are not described.

narration.text: king Limhi had made an end of speaking to his people
he told his people all the things concerning their brethren
he caused that Ammon should stand up before the multitude
And he also rehearsed unto them the last words which king Benjamin had taught them, and explained them to the people of king Limhi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Ammon’s account of earlier events is reported speech, not a separate present-time scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Zeniff or King Benjamin as physically present.
Do not invent the words spoken by Limhi or Ammon.

title: The multitude is dismissed
summary: After Ammon finishes, Limhi dismisses the multitude and directs them to return to their homes.

explicit_facts.text: After Ammon finishes, Limhi dismisses the multitude and causes each person to return to their own house.

unspecified_visual_details: The meeting place and the homes' appearance.

title: The plates are brought before Ammon
summary: The king has the plates containing his people's record brought before Ammon to read. After Ammon reads the record, the king asks whether he can interpret languages, and Ammon says he cannot.

explicit_facts.text: The king causes the plates containing his people's record, dating from their departure from Zarahemla, to be brought before Ammon for him to read.
After Ammon reads the record, the king asks whether he can interpret languages, and Ammon tells him he cannot.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ammon reads the record brought before him.
unspecified_visual_details: The plates' material and appearance; the setting and furnishings.

narration.text: he caused that the plates which contained the record of his people from the time that they left the land of Zarahemla, should be brought before Ammon, that he might read them.
Now, as soon as Ammon had read the record, the king inquired of him to know if he could interpret languages, and Ammon told him that he could not.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Ammon's answer is reported indirectly; the verses supply no verbatim dialogue.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent direct speech for the king or Ammon.

title: The king recounts the journey
summary: The king tells someone that he sent forty-three of his people into the wilderness to find Zarahemla and seek deliverance from bondage. They were lost for many days, did not find Zarahemla, and returned after traveling among many waters and discovering a land covered with bones and ruins.
characters: An unnamed person addressed by the king

explicit_facts.text: The king says he sent forty-three of his people into the wilderness to find Zarahemla and appeal to their brethren for deliverance from bondage.
The group was lost for many days, did not find Zarahemla, and returned to their land after traveling among many waters.
They discovered a land covered with human and animal bones and ruins of buildings; the king says it had been peopled by a very numerous people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The king speaks to another person while recounting an earlier expedition.
unspecified_visual_details: The speakers' appearances and the setting of their conversation are not described.
The expedition's route and the discovered land's precise appearance are not described.

prohibited_inventions: Do not name the king or the person he addresses from these verses alone.

title: Limhi asks about translation
summary: Limhi tells Ammon that a group brought engraved gold plates, breastplates, and damaged swords. He says no one in the land can interpret the plates, asks about translation, and expresses a desire to learn the cause of a people's destruction.

explicit_facts.text: A group brought twenty-four engraved plates of pure gold as testimony that what they had said was true.
The group also brought large, perfectly sound breastplates of brass and of copper.
The group brought swords with perished hilts and blades cankered with rust.
Limhi says no one in the land can interpret the language or engravings on the plates and recalls asking Ammon whether he could translate.
Limhi asks whether Ammon knows anyone who can translate and wants to learn about the people connected with the records and the cause of their destruction.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Limhi may be shown addressing Ammon.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise shapes of the artifacts and the form of the engravings.

title: Ammon describes a seer
summary: Ammon tells a king of a man who can translate ancient records, explains the interpreters and the term seer, and identifies the king in Zarahemla as the man commanded to do this.

explicit_facts.text: Ammon tells the king of a man who can translate ancient records and says the interpreters are a gift from God.
Ammon says that a person commanded to look in the interpreters is called a seer.
Ammon identifies the king of the people in Zarahemla as the man commanded to do these things.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ammon speaks to the king he addresses.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and the appearances of Ammon and the king are not described.

spoken_dialogue.speaker: Ammon

spoken_dialogue.text: And behold, the king of the people who are in the land of Zarahemla is the man that is commanded to do these things,

title: The king and Ammon discuss a seer
summary: The king says a seer is greater than a prophet. Ammon says a seer is also a revelator and prophet. The account continues with teachings about what a seer can know and what man may do through faith.

explicit_facts.text: The king says a seer is greater than a prophet.
Ammon says a seer is a revelator and a prophet, and that a man may receive great power from God.
A seer can know things past and future and make hidden or otherwise unknown things known.
God has provided a means for man, through faith, to work mighty miracles and become a great benefit to his fellow beings.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The king and Ammon may be shown conversing.
unspecified_visual_details: Their appearances, gestures, and surroundings are not described.

things which are past, and also of things which are to come,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The king’s and Ammon’s words are reported indirectly; the verses provide no direct-speech quotation.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a vision, miracle, divine appearance, or revealed event as occurring in this scene.

title: The king rejoices
summary: After Ammon finishes speaking, the king rejoices and gives thanks to God. He speaks of the plates and interpreters, praises the Lord's works, says people will not seek wisdom, and compares them to a wild flock.

explicit_facts.text: Ammon finishes speaking; the king rejoices exceedingly and gives thanks to God.
The king says the plates contain a great mystery and the interpreters were prepared to unfold mysteries.
The king praises the Lord's works and says people will not seek wisdom.
The king compares people to a wild flock fleeing its shepherd.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The king appears joyful as he gives thanks.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, clothing, gestures, and whether the plates or interpreters are visible.
